title: Noir week, iii
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Wednesday. The bait shack as a waterfront dive. Gully as a bartender who doesn't have a name this week either. A drink that is coffee.

panels.composition: The shack, lit low, drawn as a dive: a bar that is the bait counter, bottles that are bait jars. GULLY behind it in a white shirt with sleeves rolled, a towel on his shoulder. The TRENCH COAT on a stool.
panels.caption: The kind of place where nobody asks your name because nobody's got one.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a bait shack drawn as a low-lit waterfront bar with bait jars as bottles, a young man in a rolled-sleeve white shirt with a towel on his shoulder behind the counter, a man in a trench coat on a stool, film-noir shadows

panels.composition: Gully sliding a mug across. Coffee. The strip can't help it.
panels.caption: He poured me the usual. The usual was coffee. It was that kind of town.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, close-up of a hand sliding a coffee mug across a wooden counter in low light

panels.composition: The two of them. Gully's mouth open — about to say something with a balloon — and no balloon. The caption covers it.
panels.caption: He said something. I wasn't listening. I was listening to the rain, which had more to say.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a bartender with his mouth open mid-sentence and a man in a trench coat not listening, no speech balloons

panels.composition: The trench coat leaving. Gully with the towel, looking at the door. Under the counter, where the dog would be: a shadow shaped like nothing.
panels.caption: I left a dollar. It was all I had. It was all it cost.

notes: Gully as a nameless bartender. The coffee. The shadow under the counter.
